extraction.name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
extraction.description: A large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research, derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. The dataset consists of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages. It includes Language Models (LM) and baseline Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models for all languages.
extraction.creator: Facebook AI Research
extraction.inLanguage: Multilingual (English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish)
extraction.citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. "MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research." arXiv preprint arXiv:2012.03411, 2020.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox and Project Gutenberg text data, which are released in the public domain. The data collection process involved downloading audiobooks, segmenting audio files into 10-20 second segments, generating pseudo-labels, retrieving transcripts from text sources, and normalizing text. For languages other than English, manual approaches were incorporated to cover audiobook text sources due to challenges in automatic extraction.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: LibriVox audiobook data and Project Gutenberg text data, both released in the public domain.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio files were downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Text normalization included NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters (punctuations, subscript/superscripts, emojis, escape symbols), hyphen handling, and apostrophe correction. Numbers in text were aligned and replaced with aligned words from pseudo-labels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio segmentation into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models and Viterbi token sequence with timestamps. Transcript retrieval involved TF-IDF similarity scoring and Smith-Waterman alignment. Filtering of candidate transcripts with WER >40% between candidate transcript and pseudo-label. Creation of train, development, and test splits ensuring no speaker overlap, gender balance, and sufficient audio hours.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Pseudo-labels were generated using beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model on acoustic models. Human verification was performed on development and test sets to correct 'clear and obvious' errors in transcripts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: wav2letter@anywhere framework for audio segmentation and pseudo-label generation. KenLM toolkit for language model training. wav2letter++ framework for training acoustic models and decoding.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation of transcripts in development and test sets to ensure high quality. WER between generated transcript and human-rated transcript was measured (e.g., English: 4.55% dev, 4.54% test).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is made freely available at http://www.openslr.org. Versioning information and deprecation policies are not explicitly discussed.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to promote open research in large-scale training of ASR systems and multilingual ASR, potentially benefiting underrepresented languages and low-resource scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential biases may arise from the selection of audiobooks and text sources, which are derived from Project Gutenberg and LibriVox. The dataset may not be representative of all dialects or socio-economic backgrounds.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to read speech from audiobooks, which may not generalize to conversational speech. Quality issues may arise from mismatches between pseudo-labels and final transcripts, especially for numbers, hyphens, and apostrophes. The dataset may not be suitable for languages with limited audiobook availability.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine Tuning for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) research. The dataset is intended for open research in multilingual ASR and large-scale training of ASR systems.
